identity.title: Toward Guidance-Free AR Visual Generation via Condition Contrastive Alignment

problem.claim: Enable guidance-free autoregressive visual generation while preserving sample quality and controllable diversity–fidelity trade-offs.

gap.claim: In autoregressive multimodal generation, classifier-free guidance creates design inconsistencies between language and visual content, conflicting with modality unification.

contributions.claim: Condition Contrastive Alignment (CCA), a fine-tuning method for guidance-free autoregressive visual generation.
CCA fine-tunes pretrained models toward the target distribution instead of altering sampling to approximate it.
The authors report links between language-targeted alignment and visual-targeted guidance, framing them as a unified research area.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CCA from guidance methods by directly fine-tuning pretrained models to fit the same distribution target.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that one epoch of CCA fine-tuning on the pretraining dataset—1% of pretraining epochs—enhanced guidance-free performance across all tested models.
The authors report that removing guided sampling cuts sampling cost by half.
The authors report that adjusting training parameters yields diversity–fidelity trade-offs similar to those of CFG.

narrative_sequence.summary: CFG is presented as important for visual sample quality.
CFG is described as inconsistent with unified language–visual design in autoregressive multimodal generation.
The paper proposes CCA, inspired by language-model alignment, and contrasts its training-based distribution fitting with sampling-time guidance.
The authors report improved guidance-free performance, halved sampling cost, and CFG-like diversity–fidelity control, followed by a claimed theoretical connection between alignment and guidance.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly contrasts sampling-time guidance with direct fine-tuning toward the same distribution target.

lessons.interpretation: Making the intervention target explicit can clarify why a proposed method addresses a design mismatch.
lessons.application: When introducing a replacement for inference-time control, state whether it changes sampling, training, or both, and identify the target distribution or behavior.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the method intentionally targets a different distribution or relies on inference-time adaptation.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the tested models, evaluation metrics, or numerical performance gains behind “significantly enhance.”
The conditions and accounting underlying the reported halving of sampling cost are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide the theoretical argument or scope supporting the claimed connection between alignment and guidance.
